diagram_math_checks.justification: Supplier def-ip-tree-probing-experiment Definition requires a finite rooted tree with edges away from o, all nonroot leaves as receivers, and each nonroot internal vertex having at least two children. The figure has V={o,v,r,s,t}, E={(o,v),(o,t),(v,r),(v,s)}: connected with 5 vertices and 4 edges, unique root paths, root outdegree 2, v indegree 1/outdegree 2, and r,s,t indegree 1/outdegree 0. Thus R={r,s,t}; no closure edge belongs to this tree.

C1={r,s}, C2={t} are nonempty receiver subsets, with arbitrary positive N1,N2 as required by the supplier. P(o,r)={(o,v),(v,r)}, P(o,s)={(o,v),(v,s)}, P(o,t)={(o,t)}. Therefore E1={(o,v),(v,r),(v,s)} and E2={(o,t)}. The supplier path-product observations are Y_r=X_ov X_vr, Y_s=X_ov X_vs in design 1 and Y_t=X_ot in design 2 (probe/design indices suppressed); shared o→v is a multicast common edge. There is no signed measurement row or orientation reversal asserted.

Carrier Definition line 34: C1 union C2=R, so every receiver is covered. The sole nonroot internal vertex v has distinct children c=r and c′=s; each receiver belongs to its own child-rooted subtree and both are in C1, so C1 splits v. Each singleton receiver set has fewer than two distinct receivers and cannot meet the distinct-child-subtree condition. The root is exempt from splitting. These are direct finite checks, independent of the illustration.
